course_name_original: Grundlagen des Gründens – Selbstständigkeit und Unternehmertum
course_name_en: Fundamentals of Starting Up – Self-Employment and Entrepreneurship
prerequisites: Basic knowledge of the development methods of one's own discipline

learning_outcomes.text: Students can perceive, name, and discuss business problem areas and potentials of their own entrepreneurship. They can constructively name individual competencies and deficits within interdisciplinary collaborations.

Students are able to constructively apply their acquired knowledge of risk and potential analysis in the iterative creation of business models for their own startups. They can efficiently and results-orientedly plan and deploy competencies within interdisciplinary collaborations.
Students can evaluate business and legal potentials and risks of entrepreneurial activity and, after a positive evaluation, apply methods for creating business models.
Students are able to design a business model for a project developed during their studies in an interdisciplinary team, specifically using the Business Model Canvas and/or the Blue Ocean strategy.
Students create innovative business models by applying their didactic and methodological repertoire in a target group-oriented and application-appropriate manner.

Students are capable of presenting business models in writing for applications and rhetorically in a target-group-appropriate and convincing manner. They can define communicative problem areas in interdisciplinary startups and apply various solution strategies for them.
Students are able to fulfill their social responsibility and their responsibility for themselves as entrepreneurs through continuous evaluation of individual actions.

syllabus_topics: Theoretical foundations of the business, legal, and planning requirements for entrepreneurial founding (by interdisciplinary working groups)
Reading, understanding, and creating business plans for entrepreneurial startups
Practical foundations of interdisciplinary communication in the context of entrepreneurial founding
teaching_methods: Reception of other media or sources
assessment_rules: The un-graded assessment in the module serves as the basis for the graded assessment. The result of the experimental work is described in the project report and presented in a presentation. The graded project report (media) should be approximately 15 pages and include illustrative, photographic, and filmic representations. The un-graded experimental work involves approximately 3 months of creative work from the context of the course.
bibliography: Alexander Osterwalder, Business Model Generation, Campus Verlag, 2011
Eric Ries: Lean Startup: Schnell, risikolos und erfolgreich Unternehmen gründen, Redline Verlag, 2012
Patrick Stähler: Das Richtige gründen. Werkzeugkasten für Unternehmer, Murmann Verlag, 2017
W. Chan Kim: Der Blaue Ozean als Strategie, Carl Hanser Verlag, 2005
